posts.note: Pharmacology article on brand vs generic escitalopram; only a follow-up-content promise.
Essay on TikTok's algorithm, Pete and Bas, and the Nutter Butter account; no forward-looking claims.
MBT visual guide part II; only a next-installment promise.
Satirical open letter; two sincere-reading lines logged (New York vote, future controversial stances).
Fictional satirical interview with a 'Bitcoin maxi'; the character's claims are not the author's and read as jokes, so none logged.
Review of a Swedish cohort study; two hedged calls about GLP-1s in addiction and AUD.
Essay on Bluesky and the AT protocol; calls about the author's own defamation suit and federated servers.
Video explainer blurb; one conditional near-truism.
2024 list of science that will change the world: MM-120, rTMS cost-effectiveness, GLP-1s.
Year-end review of unfinished drafts; mostly own-content statements plus a Talkiatry jab.
Guest piece by Chris Aiken (deadpan satire on Gotzsche and Bhattacharya); Gotzsche's seven 'pearls' are third-party claims, not forecasts, and were not logged.
Travel dispatch from Japan; no forward-looking claims.
Review of a phase 2b psilocybin trial; regulatory and trial calls plus a Radial/Neurolief 'soon' item.

statements.quote: There is more on this thread to pull…stay tuned!
statements.context: Closing line of an article on Lexapro vs generic escitalopram (a Chinese RCT with suicide events, an adolescent placebo-controlled trial). The author promises further newsletter coverage of this thread.
statements.note: Own-newsletter promise of a follow-up article; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: In the next installment, we will describe how to address these “too-hot” modes in your life!
statements.context: Part II of a visual guide to mentalization-based treatment (MBT). After describing the 'too hot' non-mentalizing modes (Psychic Equivalence, Teleological Mode), the author promises a next installment on how to address them.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: As a resident of the state of New York, my vote will do very little
statements.context: Satirical open letter offering the newsletter for acquisition by billionaires, written before the November 2024 US presidential election. The author says his New York vote will change very little, implying the New York result is not in doubt.
statements.note: Borderline; near-truism that New York is not a swing state. Satirical post, but this line reads sincere.

statements.quote: We (the royal we) have stood resolutely against this or that, and we are likely to do so again.
statements.context: Same satirical open letter. The author says the newsletter has taken controversial political stances since July 1, 2022 and expects to do so again.
statements.note: Own-newsletter behavior; CONTROL candidate. Satirical framing, but the claim reads sincere.

statements.quote: We have written about the potential for GLP-1 medicines (Brand names Ozempic, Monjauro, Wegovy, Zepbound, etc.) to reduce, among other things, my personal problems of diabetes and obesity and, maybe, help with addiction.
statements.context: Opening of an article on a Swedish registry cohort study in JAMA Psychiatry (227,866 people with alcohol use disorder). The author restates the newsletter's earlier hedged view that GLP-1 drugs may help with addiction, beyond diabetes and obesity.
statements.note: Borderline; restatement of an earlier hedged call. The author spells Mounjaro as 'Monjauro'.

statements.quote: Alcohol use disorder has been difficult to treat, but it may be that semeglutide, liraglutide, hold promise as both safer and more effective treatments in subsequent evaluations.
statements.context: Conclusion of the same article. The cohort study found semaglutide and liraglutide cut alcohol-related hospitalization more than approved AUD drugs, which also raised suicide-attempt risk (aHR 1.15). The author expects later evaluations to support GLP-1s as safer and more effective AUD treatments.
statements.confidence_phrase: it may be that ... hold promise
statements.note: Hedged compound call: safer and more effective than approved AUD medications.

statements.quote: It may end up being the first defamation case to feature Bluesky Social and its “forever” AT protocol!
statements.context: Essay on Bluesky Social's growth (about 1 million new users daily) and the AT protocol. The author has an active defamation lawsuit against Esther Haddad and John Doe co-defendants over harassment on Bluesky; he expects it may be the first defamation case to feature Bluesky and the AT protocol.
statements.note: About the author's own lawsuit.

statements.quote: your author might be the first person to demonstrate that in court
statements.context: Same essay. The author calls Bluesky the most 'built for legal discovery' social media platform ever (every action is public and permanent) and expects to be the first to demonstrate that in court through his defamation suit.
statements.note: About the author's own lawsuit.

statements.quote: But judging by how humanity likes to act, I will not be the last.
statements.context: Same essay, the sentence after the claim that the author might be the first to demonstrate Bluesky's legal-discovery nature in court. He predicts other defamation cases built on Bluesky/AT protocol records will follow.

statements.quote: These can all live on private servers or hybrid servers in the future.
statements.context: Same essay. Medical and academic communities from old Twitter have been reborn on Bluesky as #medsky and #academicsky; the author says these communities can live on private or hybrid servers in the future under the federated AT protocol.
statements.note: Borderline; capability claim about the federated architecture.

statements.quote: It's also true that if all the healthcare payments collapse, we're all going to be worse off.
statements.context: Short post introducing a video explainer that compares flood insurance with drug pricing and health insurance, amid public anger at UnitedHealthcare and insurance denials. The author warns that a collapse of healthcare payments would leave everyone worse off.
statements.note: Conditional; near-truism.

statements.quote: We have some science published in 2024 that I think will make a huge impact in the future
statements.context: Framing sentence of the '2024 Edition' list of science that will change the world: MM-120 (LSD) for GAD, a Dutch rTMS cost-effectiveness RCT, and GLP-1 trial results. The author expects these findings to have a large future impact and wants to speed adoption (he cites an average 17-year lag).
statements.note: Umbrella claim over three findings; each finding has its own statement.

statements.quote: They have already dosed the first patient in phase 3. More data is forthcoming, but a single-dose treatment for GAD is a huge deal.
statements.context: Item 1 of the list: Mind Medicine's MM-120 (proprietary LSD) for generalized anxiety disorder. Phase 2b reported 78% clinical response (100 and 200 µg) and 50% remission (100 µg) at Week 4; the first phase 3 patient is dosed. The author expects more data and calls a single-dose GAD treatment a huge deal.
statements.note: Author discloses work with the team and <1000 shares; he adds that skepticism is warranted until larger real-world samples exist.

statements.quote: This will make it—I hope—much harder for health plans to deny this care.
statements.context: Item 2: a Dutch pragmatic multicenter RCT (Dalhuisen et al., Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica) found rTMS dominant over next-step medication in treatment-resistant depression (QALYs 0.618 vs 0.545, lower costs). The author expects this causal evidence to make it harder for health plans to deny TMS coverage.

statements.quote: These drugs are knocking down every plausible large-scale trial we throw their way. It’s hopeful. “More to come,” I say, both in these specific drugs and, I hope, in drug development more broadly.
statements.context: Item 3: semaglutide (Novo Nordisk) and tirzepatide (Eli Lilly) succeeding in large trials for cardiovascular mortality, knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea. The author expects more positive results for these drugs and hopes for the same in drug development more broadly.
statements.note: Compound: these specific drugs and drug development broadly.

statements.quote: It gets more spicy from there, but sadly, it isn’t done… and thus won’t happen in the waning hours of 2024.
statements.context: Year-end review of unfinished 2024 articles, posted Dec 31, 2024. About the draft 'Medical Boards Won't Save Us': the author says it is not done and will not be published in the remaining hours of 2024.
statements.note: Trivial own-newsletter statement; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Medical Boards Won't Save Us
statements.context: Title of an unfinished 2024 article in the year-end review. The author's stance is that medical licensing boards will not protect the public from professional misconduct despite elaborate licensure processes; he cites his own experience of a state medical board investigation.
statements.note: Borderline; general stance carried by an article title, not a dated call.

statements.quote: Maybe I’ll get an article out of it, but 2024 won’t be that year.
statements.context: About the unfinished 'Even If The Heavens Fall' article on ethics and the Trolley Problem, tied to the author's maintenance-of-certification reading. He may write it later but not in 2024.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: They raised $130M in their Series C…and will in theory now do value based something? With glassdoor reviews like this, what could go wrong?
statements.context: About the unfinished 'Building Nothing Out of Something' article on Talkiatry, a telehealth company the author says hires good psychiatrists but keeps them off high-acuity cases. After a $130M Series C, Talkiatry will supposedly move to value-based care; the sarcastic 'what could go wrong?' signals the author expects problems.
statements.note: Sarcastic; implied negative expectation about Talkiatry's value-based pivot.

statements.quote: I suspect Dr. Bhattacharya will require more clinical evidence if3 he takes the reins at NIH.
statements.context: Guest article by Chris Aiken, MD (Carlat Report editor) on Peter Gotzsche's psychiatric piece in the Journal of the Academy of Public Health, launched by Jay Bhattacharya, Trump's nominee for NIH director. Aiken expects Bhattacharya to require more clinical evidence if he takes the NIH post; the editor's footnote 3 changes 'if' to 'When'.
entities: Journal of the Academy of Public Health
statements.note: Guest author's claim in a deadpan satirical piece; the author (editor) adopts the premise via the footnote 'When…'.

statements.quote: Editors note: When…
statements.context: Footnote 3 by the editor (Owen Muir) on Chris Aiken's line 'if he takes the reins at NIH'. The author corrects 'if' to 'When', asserting that Jay Bhattacharya, nominated by Donald Trump in December 2024, will become NIH director.
statements.note: Call carried by a one-word footnote; the author expects Bhattacharya to be confirmed as NIH director.

statements.quote: We have learned, since then, that functional unblinding will be THE issue on which these compounds and their administration protocols are judged.
statements.context: Review of Ross et al. (General Hospital Psychiatry, 2025), a Usona-sponsored phase 2b trial of psilocybin vs niacin in 35 patients with life-threatening illness that did not assess blinding. After the FDA advisory committee on MDMA, the author predicts functional unblinding will be the decisive issue on which psychedelic compounds and protocols are judged.

statements.quote: These authors demonstrated that psilocybin may offer hope for human depression at the end of life, and I look forward to the phase III trial.
statements.context: Closing of the same review. Psilocybin cut HADS depression more than niacin placebo at 6-7 weeks (d = 1.12), but the crossover-only comparison showed no difference. The author says psilocybin may help end-of-life depression and expects a phase III trial.
statements.confidence_phrase: may offer hope ... I look forward to
statements.note: Compound: hedged efficacy view plus the expectation that a phase III trial happens.

statements.quote: They include Spravato, Nightware, eTNS, PRISM Neurofeedback, soon, eCOT-AS by Neurolief, TMS, Accelerated TMS, and fMRI-guided SAINT TMS.
statements.context: Promotional section 'Get Healthcare At Radial' at the end of the post, listing treatments offered at Radial, where the author works. eCOT-AS by Neurolief is flagged as coming 'soon'.
statements.note: Own organizations (Radial, Neurolief); CONTROL candidate.
